what_it_does: Post-quantum cryptography is encryption designed to resist attacks from quantum computers; CRYSTALS-Kyber is a leading candidate standard. At the heart of this cryptography is modulo reduction—a mathematical operation (computing remainder after division) that must run extremely fast in hardware. The classical Barrett algorithm for modulo reduction creates oversized intermediate numbers, preventing high clock speeds and throughput. This paper introduces CRIS-b, a novel algorithm that avoids this size expansion and supports both positive and negative numbers, enabling faster cryptographic hardware implementations.
